title: AI Lessons for Younger Students
lede: Ready-to-teach lessons about AI for children, with no screens for the students. In 40 minutes or less, students sort, count, guess and test with paper and with each other, and the whole class pulls it together at the end.
objectives: Tell the difference between a tool that always does the same thing and an AI system that finds patterns and makes guesses.
Explain that people build AI systems and choose the examples they are built from.
Show how an AI system can produce something that sounds right and is still wrong, and say how a person can check.
Describe AI in precise words: it sorts, predicts and guesses from patterns; it is not a person.
Decide when to ask an adult, and what should happen to the information they share with apps and devices.

threads.name: What AI is (and isn't)
threads.line: Spot AI in everyday life, and tell a tool that follows fixed steps from one that guesses from patterns.

threads.name: How AI learns
threads.line: People choose the examples, and the system finds patterns in them. More, more varied and more correct examples give better guesses.

threads.name: When AI is wrong (and how we check)
threads.line: AI can sound sure and still be wrong. Students practise checking, and ask who could be missed.

threads.name: AI-made content
threads.line: Pictures, texts and voices can be made with AI. Students look for clues and ask why it matters who made something.

threads.name: Me and AI
threads.line: What apps and devices do with what we share, who decides what we see, and when to ask an adult.

bands.line: Short lessons with objects, pictures and movement, for children who are just starting to read.
The main focus of the track, for students who can read a short text and work in pairs on their own.

how_it_works: Every lesson has a teacher page you can read in about ten minutes, and a student PDF to print.
Students work on their own first, then in pairs, and then the whole class pulls it together: individual, pairs, all.
You lead, and the students do most of the work. Suggested wording helps where the words matter, for example to describe what a machine does without making it sound like a person.
Every lesson ends with a closing question that each student answers before leaving.
The lessons work on their own or in order. Pick what suits your class.
what_you_need: A printer. The student PDFs are A4, fit US Letter and print well in black and white.
A board, and a projector for the lessons with a short teacher demo of an AI tool.
No devices or accounts for students. In this track, children never use AI themselves.
About ten minutes to read the teacher page, plus the preparation it lists.
